title: Recording with Sharkey in New Orleans at the Roosevelt Hotel
summary: He recorded a session with Sharkey locally at the Roosevelt Hotel, supervised by the Decca founder, and collectors still seek those records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: area. He wouldn't use Bill Bourgeois. Isn't that funny? I don't know why. Yeah. But you know, it always struck me as strange. I think Bill was a little hurt, you know. He's working with Schalke and Schalke with the New Zealand on the record, maybe. I don't know. Bill played a pretty good player in the two. Well, you recorded with Schalke too, didn't you?

Well, that was done down here. We made a record down here. And one side of that was Yes She Does, No She Don't, and I forget the Everybody Lows My Baby or something like that was on the other side. Yeah, I remember that. We made that in the Roosevelt Hotel. And strangely enough, the guy who founded Decca was the guy who recorded that thing. It was the name Cap. Dave or Jack, one of the two. Yeah, he was in, he was the one that made the session. I remember that.
Trevor Richards has something. See people collecting your records still.
Can I buy them back? Like TV rights, huh?
Yeah. I hate to tell you, but you sound pretty good.
